utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are no preliminaries. Therefore, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Radojcic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Ivetic will now continue his examination. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, colonel.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to deal with one more matter from your witness statement, which is D535 in e-court. I'd like to turn to page 11 in the English and page 16 in the Serbian, and paragraph 61.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I receive a copy of my statement in Serbian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With the help of the usher, I would ask that the hard copy that was used yesterday be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you be so kind as to repeat the number of the paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 61, which is page 16 in the Serbian, page 11 in the English. Here, sir, you talk about eliminating paramilitaries from the ZO and that you asked the Main Staff to send help to that end. When you talk about "help," what help did the Main Staff of the VRS send?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may, before I answer directly to your question, I wanted to explain what kind of paramilitary unit it was. In the area of my brigade, there was a paramilitary formation commanded by Branislav aka Brne. They numbered some 60 to 65 men. Formally speaking, they were part of the adjacent Igman Brigade. However, given the fact that most members of that unit lived in Ilidza, they spent most of their time in the area of my brigade. There were daily problems with them, and for the most part it involved racketeering of caterers, shops, and the latest thing that happened was arson. A fire was set in a catering facility. Since I did not have any authority over them, they were not within my brigade establishment, I couldn't do anything. My military police from my brigade could intervene, but they had relatives among the members of my police brigade and it limited the efficiency of MP's actions. Being aware of that fact, I turned directly to the chief of the Main Staff, General Mladic. In a telephone conversation, I told him about the problems with the paramilitary formation. He had a principled position about such paramilitary formations. It was such that he considered all members of paramilitary formations to include them in the VRS in order to join the struggle of the Serbian people. However, they refused it, and that is why he promised assistance. Indeed, he sent parts of the Protection Regiment to dealt with it in a single afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: In a single morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Parts of the unit who, and that is to say members of it who did not do anything illegal, they individually deployed them to the Ilidza and Igman Brigades. As of that moment, there were no other paramilitary formations in the area of my brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say the protection regiment was sent to deal with it, could you explain what that means?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that one of the elite units of the VRS was sent in. They were authorised to deal with it in an efficient manner and they had the skills required to do so. In other words, they could completely disband the unit in a very short time, and as of that moment on, as I said, it no longer existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to draw your attention to the time-period of May 1995. Do you recall during this time-period when NATO aircraft under the direction of the UN began operations in -- in and around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your brigade did in reference to UNPROFOR personnel at that time when these NATO planes began conducting air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said already, in the area of my brigade there were Military Observers and UNPROFOR members. The Military Observers, a few days before the NATO air campaign, withdrew to their base, whereas the UNPROFOR members remained in their positions in the area of the brigade. I have to say that in the area of defence of the Ilidza Brigade, there were two UNPROFOR units. The first unit was from an airborne regiment from the French army. They were in the Sumarska School building along the separation with the 104th Motorised Brigade of the Army of BH. There were some 20 of them. The other UNPROFOR units in the area of my brigade was from the Ukrainian Battalion. They were billeted in the Energoinvest compound. It was a large factory that was in our territory. They too had some 20 men. When I received an order to place UNPROFOR members under my control as POWs - because at that point in -- of time we were de facto in a state of war with NATO and its air forces, thus they became our prisoners of war. First of all, I spoke to the Ukrainian Battalion commander. I think his name was Colonel Valery Sklai [phoen]. I told him that the situation was changed and that they were no longer UNPROFOR members overseeing the troops but that as of that moment on they were our POWs because of that state of war with NATO. He agreed, and he said, "I am aware of the situation but let us come up with a situation so as to avoid any problems for the personnel." I agreed and I told him that we would deal with that problem in a mutually satisfactory way. He suggested -- well, first he asked that he be allowed to withdraw his unit to the base in Sarajevo in the former Marsal Tito Barracks. I told him I couldn't do that because the order I received from my superior command did not allow for that. Then he said, "Fine. I will leave behind my APCs next to your military police building and the personnel will be in the containers where they had been until then." The weapons were to be separated, placed in a different facility. I said that it was acceptable and that in the same way I could implement my order and preserve the dignity of his personnel. Then I went to the French Battalion representatives. They numbered about 20, around one platoon. They were close to the base in the Sarajevo airport. I found the platoon commander. I spoke to him and I told him the same I did to the Ukrainian Battalion commander. He told me that according to the rules of service of the French army, the Foreign Legion is not to surrender without fight and they said that they were prepared to fight, if necessary. However, given the -- the fact that they were outnumbered, he asked me not to do that because they were not going to put any obstacles in my way in the course of implementing my order. They laid down their weapons, which were placed in one of the rooms. They promised not to leave their base. They used communication links to stay in touch with their battalion command. I offered all kind of assistance to them in terms of providing food and water, and I asked them for their security not to move about. If there was indeed some serious need to do so due to illness or something else, I asked that I be informed so that they could be escorted by my military policemen to wherever they wanted to go. In that way, I could provide security for them because the situation among civilians and members of the brigade was very tense and there could have been incidents. That is how we tackled the problem, and luckily enough the issue on hand was dealt with on a more senior level shortly afterwards. I think it was one of the successful tasks which I implemented. The French Battalion commander, Colonel Kiel [phoen] if I remember well, came to visit me and he told me something like this, I'll try to recollect his words: "Colonel, sir, your fair treatment of the members of the French Battalion did not go unnoticed and we will not forget it." I took it as a great compliment. Later on he even presented me with a monograph of the regiment with a dedication. Unfortunately I do not have the book with me, but if the Chamber found it necessary I would be willing to forward it. He particularly stressed my professionalism and an exceptionally fair treatment in a very serious situation for both sides. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify, sir, in relation to the weapons and side-arms of the various UNPROFOR units, the French and the Ukrainian ones in your zone, were they -- did the UNPROFOR personnel continue to have access to the same at all?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. First of all, I wanted to say that I did not disarm the officers. They kept their side-arms but they took out the bullets from them and handed them over. Their personal weapons were left with them, and if I believe it correctly under the Geneva Conventions officers are guaranteed the right to keep their side-arms. As for any infantry long-barrelled weapons, it was put in a separate room and locked so that the soldiers did not have access to it. The key of the room was with their commanders. It was a gentleman's agreement, a show of trust between me and the UNPROFOR commanders unit, both Ukrainian and the French one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Colonel, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Ivetic. Mr. Radojcic you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Groome. Mr. Groome is counsel for the Prosecution and you'll find him to your right. Mr. Groome, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And good morning, Colonel Radojcic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to begin by asking you some questions about the giving of your statement for this case. Now can we go to the first page of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think we have D535 on our screens. If we can perhaps just go to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now it says here that you were interviewed on the 24th of May, 2013 and the 23rd of February, 2014. Do you affirm that those were the days that you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now prior to the preparation of this statement, were these the only days that you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the document indicates that you were interviewed by Milenko Dundjer. Did Mr. Dundjer interview you on both of these days?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first interview took place in Novi Sad, where I reside. That is when we met. The second more detailed interview was on the 23rd of February in his office in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And the document also indicates that Boris Zorko also interviewed you. Was he present on both days?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was present during the second interview in the Belgrade office.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now did one or the other of these men take a leading role in the interview process?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leading role in the process was in the hands of attorney-at-law Mr. Dundjer. Boris Zorko served as secretary; in other words, he was typing my statement into the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now was there anyone else who's not mentioned on this document who played a role in the interview of you on these two days?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, on the 21st of June we were provided with a note summarising some details about meetings you had with the Defence team after you arrived here in The Hague. It states that you met with them on five days from the 15th to the 19th of June. Does that agree with your recollection of what's happened since you've come to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were in daily contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It also says in that document that "proofing is ongoing." So my question to you is: Did you meet with anyone from the Defence team after the 19th of June?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 19th of June, I went back to Novi Sad because there was a break in the proceedings. I returned the next Tuesday, when I met with Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now while in The Hague, either the first time before you went back or the second time, did you meet any other witnesses in this case?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were in the same hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of all of the other people that you know to be witnesses in this case who you met after you arrived in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one was Milos, I can't recall his last name. The second person is Stojan Veljovic. The third person who was there for one day only was Mr. Tusevljak. When I left, he went back to Sarajevo the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I told you the name Skrba, would that refresh your name as to the name of Milos?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Milos Skrba.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now it appears that your Karadzic statement, which you signed on the 9th of December 2012, was used as a basis for the creation of the Mladic -- of your statement for this case. Am I correct in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in my review of the two statements, I see that some of the evidence that you provided to the Karadzic chamber has been removed and some additional information or evidence has been added. I want to look at the evidence that has been removed. Now, can I ask that we go in your Mladic statement, which is on the screen, can we go to page 16 in the original and page 12 of the English. Okay. To make my point, can you tell me what is the number of the paragraph, of the last paragraph on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we please advance to the next page of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is the number of the first paragraph on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So it would seem that paragraphs 67 and 68 have been removed. Now, could we please go to the -- the version of your statement that was tendered in the Karadzic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 1D02128. And the paragraph that I'm interested in are on page 14 in the original and page 11 of the English. Okay. There in the original we can see paragraph 67 and the first half of paragraph 68. That's somehow disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now I think we can see the parts that I want to ask you about. Now, paragraph 67 deals with the relationship between the -- the Main Staff and republican civil authorities. I'm more interested in paragraph 68. Now this paragraph deals directly with count 11 of the indictment in this case. It is directly relevant the question the Chamber will have to consider, and count 11 charges General Mladic with taking UN personnel hostage between the 26th of May and the 19th of June, 1995. The first line of the paragraph that has been removed from the statement says: "On about 25 May 1995, my brigade received the order from General Mladic to block and disarm UNPROFOR, namely the Ukrainian and French Battalions, which were in my zone of responsibility." Now, my first question at this point is simply limited to whether or not you acknowledge that this evidence which was adduced in the Karadzic case has been removed from your statement in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object as it misstates the evidence, Your Honour. We just led that evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About -- could you then please point us exactly to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just -- I believe the witness from what I can tell yesterday speaks English.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we confirm that you do speak and read English; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I thought I saw the witness reading the transcript yesterday. I'm concerned that any lengthy now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No -- yes, okay. You do not understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, could I just -- Mr. Ivetic, you raised an objection. The only thing I'm asking you at this moment, not to further explain but to exactly give us the source you apparently were referring --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- to in terms of pages and lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Temporary transcript page 4 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just led it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Temporary transcript page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Lines 2 to the end of my direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. We'll have to ask the witness to briefly leave the courtroom. Could you follow the usher for a moment. Could I ask the witness, what is on -- Witness, Witness, could you please put on your earphones. What appears on your screen to the right from here to the left. What does appear there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the screen which is on my right-hand side, I can see the English version of my statement. To its left is the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have got two screens. You are talking now about you see on the right screen; is that correct? And then that is a split-screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell me --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The right screen is split. On the right side, there is the English version and on the left side is the Serbian version. On the left-hand side screen, I see what is probably the transcript of this -- of these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've answered my question. Thank you. Would you please follow the usher for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could the witness remain stand by. Mr. Ivetic, it seems that the issue is whether the specific reference to General Mladic was led as evidence. You said it misstates the evidence. I think Mr. Groome was focusing primarily on Mr. Mladic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That wasn't the question he asked, Your Honour. If he asked that question I would not have objected. But he said that this evidence, i.e., the factual scenario from paragraph 68, was removed from this witness's testimony and statement and that's not correct. The gentleman testified for several pages on the transcript on that very topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said the first line of the paragraph reads: "On or about 25th of May 1995, my brigade received the order from General Mladic to block and disarm UNPROFOR." My first question is: Do you acknowledge that this evidence, referenced to General Mladic, which was adduced through you in the Karadzic case has now been removed from your evidence in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Specific reference to General Mladic giving an order. Is this evidence, is that the -- you consider that anywhere in all those pages you find a reference to this order stemming from General Mladic himself personally?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I thought he did. Let me just take one quick look, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I asked for the source. Perhaps you search for the word "Mladic" or for "commander" or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The reference to Mladic on the phone was just -- the question just before that, so I do not see Mladic specifically referenced in the -- I -- I apologise. I thought that the telephone conversation with Mladic was in relation to this question. It was in the question prior. Here it just says "received an order" at page 4, line 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it did not misstate the evidence. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom again. And would you be very cautious next time, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, let me repeat the most pertinent part of my question to you. The first line of the paragraph that has been removed, paragraph 68 of the Karadzic statement, says: "On about 25 May 1995, my brigade received the order from General Mladic to block and disarm UNPROFOR, namely the Ukrainian and French Battalions, which were in my zone of responsibility." And again my question at this stage is simply limited to whether or not you acknowledge that this evidence was removed from the statement that was tendered in this case, the case against General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is that this is a printing error and quite simply Mr. Zorko during the typing skipped these two paragraphs. Otherwise, there's no reason to give up on this all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that there has been an inadvertent removal of paragraphs 67 and 68 from your statement in this case.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying this because of the following. If we look at the last version, we we'll 66 and 69. Had somebody wanted to remove paragraphs 67 and 68, he would not have continued with number 69. He would have numbered the paragraph a 67 had this been a conscious intention, so you wouldn't have even have noticed. Obviously this is a printing error or typing error.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the fact -- your evidence that this is an inadvertent removal is a conclusion your drawing because a person who wanted to remove it and wanted to hide that fact would have done a better job than we've seen here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- objection denied. Mr. Groome is at this moment verifying whether he well understood the evidence as given by the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please answer it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that this is a printing error. The version of my statement for President Karadzic had the following sequence, 66, 67, 68, 69, whereas the version --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of my statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- you've explained that already. All I'm asking you now is what you're telling us, this answer, that's a conclusion that you're drawing. You don't -- you're saying this was never discussed. Am I correct in saying there was never a discussion between you and Mr. Dundjer or Mr. Zorko about the removal of paragraphs 67 and 68?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you review the statement before you signed it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you acknowledge that the evidence contained in paragraph 68 would be important evidence in this case. Do you appreciate that fact?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now can I ask you -- while we have it on the screen, can I ask you to read paragraph 68, and when you get to the bottom of the page indicate that so we can advance the page so you can read the entirety of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now we can have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could please advance the page. Perhaps in both versions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now my question to you is whether after having read it do you affirm that it is truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if I were to take the time to ask you the several questions it would take to -- to lead this evidence, would you give answers that were substantially the same?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, the topic that's been dealt in paragraph 68 was raised this morning by Mr. Ivetic, and you gave an explanation that went several pages in the transcript. And my question to you is: Do you acknowledge that nowhere in that long description and detailed description of this event did you ever say that you received the order to -- to stop and disarm the UNPROFOR, that you received this order from General Mladic? You never said that here this morning, did you?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not mention that for a simple reason. This order came down the chain of command; that is to say, General Mladic's order did not arrive to me directly as brigade commander. Rather, it came through the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and that is how it was sent down to the brigade. That's why I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So was it a conscious decision this morning not to mention the name of General Mladic because you say now you received this order through your chain of command?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't conscious. I just wanted to be more precise in my answer. I wanted to be more precise in my answer. It is true that this order came from General Mladic through the command of the SRK.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, sir, isn't it a fact that the reason it's not in your statement, the reason you didn't mention it this morning because in your view that particular piece of evidence is unhelpful to the Mladic Defence? Isn't that the truth of what just happened?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object as to the foundation of this witness knowing what is helpful to the Mladic Defence or not. That's, I believe, a decision for defence attorneys --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection denied, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't done consciously. It was just done for the sake of precision. General Mladic's position on this question is very well known, and I hope that he never concealed it either. After all, it was a generally known thing about General Mladic's position after UNPROFOR bombed our positions; that is to say, this is information that was even carried in the media. So there's no reason to try to find some wish in my answer to conceal something. On the contrary, I want to say everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution wants to tender paragraphs -- missing paragraphs, paragraphs 67 and 68. I can do that by tendering the entire statement, but I have asked Ms. Stewart to prepare just a four-page document. It has the two signature pages plus the two relevant pages, if that suits the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be more appropriate. But before deciding, I would like to hear from Mr. Ivetic what --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours. This was our 65 ter number. We didn't -- never meant to hide this. I think you should have the whole statement so you can see the comparisons of the documents to see what in fact what the witness described as to his belief of how these paragraphs ended up not in the Mladic statement. I think it provides context, so I want the whole statement in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I have no objection to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole statement in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So then I would tender, if that's acceptable to the Chamber, 65 ter 1D02128.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether the number -- could you please check on your screen whether the number is the number you mentioned Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's 1D02128, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see a 9 which.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we now have the accurate number on our screens. Madam Registrar, 1D02128 receives number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P6611, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6611 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before we leave this matter I'm informed by Ms. Stewart that the document uploaded by the Defence does have redactions. Can Mr. Ivetic please explain what those are before we move from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can, Your Honour. This is the statement that was introduced in the Karadzic case with redactions that I assume were ordered by the Karadzic chamber. We did not alter the document. We presented the document that was used as evidence in the Karadzic case, so we uploaded it in that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. It's paragraphs 107 and 125 that are redacted. May I suggest that we leave things as they stand and I will during the break check and see rather than make an assumption about what happened with those redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We do not know about the reasons for the redactions, so if you would first try to find out and then if it changes your position we'd like to hear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Radojcic, in your long description of what happened between yourself and the Ukrainian and French detachments, UNPROFOR detachments, you made it sound as if there was maybe some type of agreement that you reached with them and I want to confirm that. Is it your evidence that the Ukrainian UNPROFOR personnel agreed to be prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were aware of the situation and the commander of the Ukrainian Battalion said to me: "I'm aware of the situation. If at all possible, can I return my men to the base in Sarajevo?" And I said, "No, from this moment onwards you are POWs of the Army of Republika Srpska and I can just agree that this be done in a dignified manner so as not to do any harm to the dignity of the Ukrainian army." And he agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please carefully listen to the question that Mr. Groome is putting to you, is whether they agreed to have been taken prisoner of war. Not whether they agreed about details of what happened in that situation, not whether they were aware of that situation, but whether they agreed that taking them, that they agreed that they were prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This situation they were not in a position to agree or disagree. I told them that they were POWs and I explained why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the same question with respect to the French. So they really had no choice in whether or not they were going to be POWs; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they had no choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now you said that the -- and you mentioned a French officer that they complimented you on their treatment. When -- when did this happen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This happened when this crisis was over, the crisis with the prisoners. He came to see me as soon as he could, and since he was aware of the situation in detail and my attitude and the attitude of my officers towards the members of the French Foreign Legion, as a token of his gratitude he said what I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now when they were freed, let's focus on the French Battalion, they left your area in a bus and they went to Belgrade; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are Military Observers. In my zone, there were no Military Observers. The members of the French Battalion had their combat vehicles. They got into these vehicles and went to base. The vehicles had been parked in front of the building where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And tell us the month and year, as best you can remember, when this French officer returned to compliment you on what had taken place during this crisis.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is May 1995. I think that this crisis went on for about ten days, and after that crisis he took the first opportunity to come and see me and we had that conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that he gave you some token of appreciation; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he gave me a monograph of his regiment, and in this book he wrote a dedication and he thanked me for my professionalism and my wish to have even the most difficult problems resolved to mutual benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One short question in the meantime, Mr. Groome. Sir, you -- before you gave your answer about May 1995, you looked into your papers in front of you. Did you find the date there? Were you looking at a specific paragraph of your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just tried to find the exact date because in my statement we have the exact date. I couldn't remember the date right now so I couldn't find it, and then my answer was that it was May 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you made an offer to provide this -- this memento. Where is it now? Do you know -- do you know actually where it is?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in my apartment in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you that after you're discharged as a witness that you provide it to the Defence so I may take a look at it. I would be interested in seeing it. And if that's possible, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very, very gladly. And if necessary, I'll send the original of the book, but could it please be returned to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to move to another topic. I see that we're very close to the break. Could we take the break a few minutes early and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just wanted to follow up on Judge Fluegge's question before we take the break. You said you just wanted to find the exact date in your statement. Did you find in it in the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom. We take a break of 20 minutes, and we'd like to see you back after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we break I can confirm that the Karadzic chamber ordered the redactions of paragraphs 107 and 125, and that resolves the matter that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any reasons known which can be discussed in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... related to paragraphs in the Karadzic indictment that had been dropped. So they were considered no longer relevant to the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Incidents that had been dropped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Whereas these paragraphs are about -- at least one of them gives a title that it's about incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are the same incidents dropped in the present case?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I only have redacted from Karadzic so I don't know what text lies underneath the redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then it may be interesting because you said we are interested in the whole of the statement. If it was not relevant in that case, it doesn't mean that it would not be relevant in this case. So if you could please try to find out. It is not considered to be a protective measure, it's just on relevance, so therefore I think this Chamber can decide on the matter as it wishes after having heard about these --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the transcript is correct: The paragraphs again are 107 and 115, and it is I that misspoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I looked at them. Perhaps we use the few minutes for the one matter; that is, the reasons for the decision on the Defence motion for protective measures for Witness GRM258 because the Chamber stills owes the reasons for that decision. The Chamber therefore will now deliver its reasons for the denial of the Defence motion for protective measures for Witness GRM258. On the 17th of April, 2014, the Defence filed a motion requesting the use of pseudonym, image, and voice distortion as well as the redaction of Witness GRM258's name and any other information in his witness statement which might reveal his identity. On the 1st of May of this year, the Prosecution filed its response, opposing the motion. On 8 May 2014, the Defence filed a request for leave to reply, attaching its reply as an annex. Following informal communication concerning the nature of the reply, on the 12th of May, 2014, during the Pre-Defence Conference, the Chamber put on record that it considered the reply to be part of the original motion, that it would not further decide on the request to reply, and it invited the Prosecution to file a response. On the 16th of May, the Prosecution filed its consolidated response, still opposing the motion. On the 19th of May, 2014, the Chamber informed the parties that it defers its decision on the motion until it has had an opportunity to further hear from the witness in person. On the 13th of June, the Chamber and the parties put questions to the witness in court. Further submissions were made by the Prosecution orally, and the Defence in written form, respectively, on the 16th of June, 2004. The Chamber has set out in a previous decision the test it applies when considering whether to grant protective measures. The Chamber refers the parties to its decision on Prosecution motion for protective measures for Witness RM115 dated the 15th of August, 2012. The Chamber considered that the witness had only expressed very general concerns about negative consequences of his anticipated testimony. With regard to incidents allegedly experienced by him, the Chamber was, based on the information provided by the witness, unable to conclude that the incidents were due to his previous testimony in the Karadzic case. Consequently, the Chamber could not draw from these incidents that testimony in this case would put the witness or his family at risk. The Chamber concluded that there's no objectively grounded risk for the security or welfare of either the witness or his family and denied the motion for protective measures for Witness GRM258. And this concludes the Chamber's reasons for its decision to deny the protective measures sought for Witness GRM258. We take a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the witness to be brought in, I briefly address the following matter. It's about the 92 ter motion related to Slobodan Tusevljak. On the 12th of May of this years the Defence filed a motion pursuant to Rule 92 ter seeking the admission of materials related to Slobodan Tusevljak; namely, A, the witness's statement given in the Karadzic case; B, a supplementary witness statement prepared for the present proceedings; and C, six associated exhibits. At this point the Chamber notes that the Defence did not attach the witness's statement given in the Karadzic case to its motion. On the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would have one moment of patience, Witness. One moment of patience. I'm just dealing with another matter. It will be finished in 30 seconds. On 26th May of this year the Prosecution filed a response not opposing the admission of the supplementary statement. It reserves its position on admission of the witness's statement given in the Karadzic case until it receives a complete, signed, and dated version of the same. On the 2nd of June, the Defence filed a request for leave to reply, which is hereby granted. The Chamber notes, however, that the reply includes a witness statement which is neither signed, nor dated, and encourages the Defence to address this issue before the witness will give his testimony before the Chamber. Having dealt with this matter -- and, again, apologies. Thank you for your patience, Mr. Radojcic. Mr. Groome will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Radojcic, in paragraphs 4 and 5 of your statement, you give evidence about the SRK being surrounded by an inner and outer ring of the ABiH 1st Corps. Now I want to ask you several questions in this regard. First, the first sentence in paragraph 5 states: "The command of my brigade had information that the SRK encircled from the outside by the BiH army. My brigade held a front line facing both the inner and outer ring." My first question is: Do you know what the source of this information was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received my duties, the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps informed me about the tactical and operative situation of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. That happened in January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the person who provided you with this information.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now in your statement you don't specify a date, so my question to you is: Is it your evidence that throughout the -- your tenure at the Ilidza Brigade, you believed that you were surrounded by an inner and outer bring of ABiH troops?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must admit that my statement was not precise. When you say encirclement, that means that you're encircled totally. My brigade was in a semi-encirclement, to be very precise. If you look at the zone of defence of the Ilidza Brigade, you will see that the only exit that my brigade had was across Rajlovac, Vogosca, and then around Sarajevo towards Pale and Lukavica. This is why I am saying that was not precise when I said encirclement because it was not a total encirclement. We were in a semi-encirclement, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well before your statement was admitted into evidence, Mr. Ivetic gave you an opportunity to correct any portion of your statement. Why did you not correct this part of your evidence then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be very precise in answering your question. I didn't think that it was so important, so I didn't pay that much attention to the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now let's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was it then your impression through the war that the semi-encirclement was by both an inner and an inner -- outer circle of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can elaborate, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. Thank you so much. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now let's not conflate your brigade situation with the situation for the entire corps. As I understand you now, you're saying that with respect to your brigade you were not encircled. You are now using a term "semi-encircled"; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you use the term "semi-encircled," you mean that you had the ability to go in and out of the brigade without crossing enemy lines; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now let's go to the other use of encirclement with respect to the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and what General Galic told you, as you've just given evidence about. Did he tell you that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps is encircled by an inner and outer ring, or did he tell you the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps is semi-encircled with an inner and outer ring?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the latter would be more correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's now your evidence that General Galic told you that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was not encircled but was semi-encircled; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Colonel Radojcic, as a military officer, there's a big, big difference between being encircled and something other than encircled, is there not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly there is a difference. However, that difference is not that drastic. If we're talking about the Ilidza Brigade, I had just one possibility to leave that zone with my unit and with the people. If Rajlovac had fallen or Vogosca for that matter, I would have been completely encircled. The front lines were narrow and the distance to the enemy was very short. It was a realistic that a hung over our heads throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But the question is you're here giving evidence under oath, and you're now saying that what's in your statement, something you reviewed and signed very recently, is not accurate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's your explanation for using the word "encirclement" when what you now say is the truth is you were semi-encircled. What's your explanation for that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The explanation is this. We had front lines facing the Muslim part of Sarajevo as well. That's why our enemies were also behind our backs. My brigade had its enemy on Mount Igman. That's why our tactical position was very difficult or rather we perceived it as an encirclement because there was just one very narrow passage leading towards the rest of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, what you're saying is now is you were not encircled but you perceived it as an encirclement; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object, Your Honours. And I would direct counsel to look at the sentence in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is that meant for me or the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm certainly aware what's in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you answer my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I get a ruling on the objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. But please, Mr. Ivetic. You make an objection, you refer me to a paragraph, so I want to read that paragraph before I give a ruling on your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the basis of your objection is not clear apart from that you object and that you advise Mr. Groome to look at paragraph 5. What now the objection is, because the question was about what the testimony of the witness is now despite what he may have said or has -- as what we find in his statement. So I do not see exactly -- Mr. Groome explores what the newest evidence now is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How he could get an answer from that by reading what is not the newest but what is in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the testimony that Mr. Groome is referring to, which begins at line 30 -- pardon me, page 30, line 16 through 21, I'm directing the attention to the last part of paragraph 5 which I believe is precisely this evidence that is being mischaracterised by new by the Prosecution's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you -- if you would take out single words then perhaps there is some corresponding things, but the main line of questioning is clear. And based on the whole of paragraph 5, I would deny the objection. Mr. Groome, could you please proceed. Perhaps you repeat the question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, my question to you is: What you're saying now, which is different from your statement, is that you were not in fact encircled but that you perceived yourself to be encircled; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. My last sentence says our brigade had communication with the rest of Republika Srpska only through Rajlovac which implies that we were not completely encircled. I agree that in the first part of the paragraph it should read that my brigade was in semi-encirclement not in encirclement. I don't know how this happened. It's a mistake. So, yes, it was a semi-encirclement. Because the last sentence in this paragraph confirms what I'm saying. The only communication of our brigade with the rest of Republika Srpska was only through Rajlovac. This was the only exit or -- that we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could now, exactly, Mr. Ivetic, this is what happens. You give a hint that the last line of paragraph 5 gives a clue to the answer. And then the witness starts interpreting the word "communication," which has -- could have many, many meanings, to be the gap in what he described again and again as an encirclement. Therefore, if there's any further objection, then before you object, you should ask the Chamber to briefly pause and then we'll consider whether or not we'll hear that objection in the presence or in the absence of the witness. Mr. Groome, whenever there's an objection, you should immediately stop and then I'll guide the parties through the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate Your Honours' guidance. I just want to again emphasise, the witness testified about this before I made my objection. And the statement in -- in -- that is signed in B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: -- has this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- leave it to my -- my guidance is there. My ruling is there. Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Colonel, let's take a closer look at paragraph 4. You say in paragraph 4, you talk about the ABiH 1st Corps having a strength between 45.000 and 100.000 combatants which were deployed in inner and outer rings. So let me ask you now with this possibly different understanding of what encirclement is, is it still your evidence that the ABiH 1st Corps had an inner ring and an outer ring of troops?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is still my statement. The main forces of the 1st Corps of the BiH army were in the inner part of Sarajevo. You can see it on the map. It's adjacent forces were behind the backs of the Ilidza and Ilijas Brigades. They were deployed in Hrasnica, Sokolovic Kolonija --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Butmir and Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- we can't see the map at the moment. Before I ask you -- I'm going to ask you to do some things with this map. Are we in agreement that a ring, like a circle, has no beginning and no end. Can we agree on the term "ring" before we proceed? Do we agree on the term?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, of course, I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now could I ask that P3 be brought to our screens. This is the Sarajevo map book. And could I ask that we go to page 54.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, Colonel Radojcic, what's going to come up on the screen is a copy of this map that we have in court. But obviously because of its size it's a little bit difficult to work with on the screen, okay? Now I was unable to work out looking at this map the rings that you describe in your statement. Before I ask you to show us those rings, please stay where you, can you confirm that this is a VRS map that includes the greater Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now with the Court's permission, I'm going to ask you to trace with the pointer these rings. Now please don't do anything until you hear my complete instruction. Once you stand up to go to the map, we cannot hear what you're saying, so I'm going to ask you not to speak. When I hold up one finger, that's going to indicate would you please trace the inner ring of troops. When I hold up two fingers, that's going to indicate that I'm asking you to trace the outer ring. Okay? Now in order for us to see this, can I ask you to go very, very slowly. We'll be able to watch a close-up of what you do on our monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, perhaps we need to -- I see there's another set of earphones there, but let's see -- no, we don't need them. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, can I ask you to stand up and now trace very slowly, let's do it three times, what you say is the inner ring of ABiH troops, okay? Sir, we can't hear you. We --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I'm going to show the inner ring. We can see an uninterrupted line containing the main forces of the BiH army. Around it were the main forces of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And now I'm going show the outer ring and let me tell you immediately that I did not invent that term "outer ring." Similarly to the modified aerial bomb, it's not completely adequate. The Ilidza Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, hold on. Just one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask the director to -- just to zoom out a bit more from the ... Can we see the map on our monitors again and see if it's zoomed out. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, can you now -- can you now trace the outer ring of Muslim forces that encircled the ABiH troops that you referred to as the outer ring of ABiH troops in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm inquiring: Are we somehow recording the encirclements? I believe it's usual practice to identify for the record what is being represented on the demonstrative exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the video, of course, is part of the record as well, so everyone could always see it. But we'll take care, if you have any concerns in that respect, Mr. Ivetic, that it will be done in such a way that there can be no doubt as to what the witness pointed at. Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Now the outer ring that you describe in your statement. The outer ring of ABiH forces. Do it quite slowly so we can follow the pointer.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please resume your seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before he does --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- I have a question. In relation to those two rings, could you indicate where your units were; in other words, the SRK corps including your brigade? Just do the circle. Don't talk. Just do the circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So from what you've just done, it then means the inner circle of the BiH did not encircle you or semi-encircle you. You encircled. Am I correct? You were therefore not encircled by two lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at the map, you will see the positions of the Ilidza Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will also see that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me, sir. That's not my question. From the lines that you drew, I see where you indicate your units to have been is outside what you say is the inner circle of the BiH units. I'm saying to you you were therefore not encircled by two -- by an inner and an outer circle of BiH. You actually encircled the inner one. Just yes or no. Do you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what about the forces that were behind my back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You -- that's not my question and you don't ask me questions. That wasn't my question. My question was just that you are encircling the inner circle of BiH; is that correct? I didn't hear what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Groome. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before that I would like to deal with the request by Mr. Ivetic --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What I'm about to do now is to -- is now to get him to do it in pen on the document that's on the screen. That was always my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: But given the size of it, I thought it would be helpful for the Chamber to see a full-sized map. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we'll now do the marking on the screen and then we have to -- I take it we have to zoom out, maximum --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I think we have the entire thing on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I may have zoomed in myself on my version.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So with the usher's assistance, could we please use a green pen so we don't confuse with the red and blue lines already on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you now -- don't touch the screen yet with that pen because as soon as you do, there will be a mark. I'm going to ask you to draw the inner circle and then put a 1 next to the inner circle and if you would just follow us what you showed on the large map. So show us the inner circle in a green line with a 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now can you do the same thing. You traced what you said was the outer ring. Can you now trace that on this map before us. And again mark 2 next to that outer ring.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. And that's -- you've made your marks. While we're here, while you have the pen on hand, could I ask you to put a dot and a letter R to show us where Rajlovac is, the location you mentioned in paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I please go to the big map because what I have on the screen is kind of blurred and the letters are too little. It's very hard for me to see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. So before we do that can I ask that we save this? So we memorialize this, could this be tendered as an exhibit, your markings? But before we do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- are there any other markings you want to make on this map to represent the outer ring of the ABiH troops?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have to apologise and say that I'm not familiar with the outer ring in detail. I was a brigade commander, not a corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have precisely -- I think in the part that was shown on the video there was another section that was indicated that I do not see on this electronic version that has been marked, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is the -- In your marking, Witness, did do exactly the same with a pen as you did on the big map before, or did you point at a portion also in, if I could say so, in the south-easterly part of this map where we also see blue and red dotted lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before me is the map with a very large-scale, 1:100.000; as to opposed to this map, and the scale there is 1:50.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I can see things far better on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a different matter. Is it true then when you were standing, did you also point at, when explaining to us where the outer ring was, also to a part of the map which is more in a south-easterly direction where we see the red and blue dotted lines as well? Is that true? Would you make that marking which you did before on the big map also the screen at this moment? Would you add that to the markings you have made until now on the screen with that same green pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't worry about -- too much about the details but that at least you cover some of it. Mr. Ivetic, is this what you had in mind? And there the witness adds a portion --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and now I believe it comports to what was done on the demonstrative exhibit and I have no objection to it being tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar this map marked by the witness would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 54 of Exhibit P3 as marked by the witness receives number P6612, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6612 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, recalling our agreement a few minutes ago that a ring had no beginning and no end, it is true that the line that you have drawn has two beginnings and two ends; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's not a ring, is it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a full ring. The term "outer ring" is imprecise. The definition of the inner ring is precise, but the definition of the outer ring is quite imprecise as obviously there were interruptions in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's a semi-ring. Is that what your evidence should be understood? Where you said there was an outer ring of ABiH troops should be understood to mean that there's such thing as a semi-ring of ABiH troops. Is that how we should understand your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I provided my statement, I relied on the term that was used throughout the war, the inner and outer rings. I do understand that the term "outer ring" is inadequate as it was interrupted. I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the gap that is at the -- at the top, the top right quadrant of that map, that's -- that opening would allow access to the Drina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So someone could drive from the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps to Zvornik and even straight on to Belgrade without ever having to cross a front line manned by ABiH troops; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the other gap that you have at the bottom left quadrant, after the operation Lukavica 93 that gave unfettered access between the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps and the Herzegovina Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now you said a few minutes ago when I asked you about these gaps, you said: "I have to apologise and say that I'm not familiar with the outer ring in detail. I was the brigade commander, not the corps commander." Now in your statement, it doesn't say that "I'm not sure about the outer ring, this is what I was told." It says quite definitively that there is an outer ring made up of 45.000 to 100.000 troops, divided between the two rings. It says quite definitively that there is an outer ring of ABiH troops. Doesn't your statement say that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your answer wasn't recorded or translated. Can I ask you to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that the manning level of the 1st Corps was between 45- and 100.000 men, depending on the period of the war, who were deployed in the outer and inner rings. In the inner ring there were the main forces of the 1st Corps. In the outer ring at Igman there were auxiliary forces of the 1st Corps of the Army of BH. That is what is contained in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now to follow up Judge Moloto's point, do you now concede that it's not the SRK that is encircled but it's the ABiH troops within the confines of Sarajevo, those are the troops that are encircled and encircled by the SRK? Do you concede that point?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you were going to ask the witness where Rajlovac was situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, we're getting a better map. I'm going to have to come back to that, if that's okay, and we have a map that I'll call up. And I think we'll be able to do it in a few minutes that -- it's a different map, though, and it will clearly show that location. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So now before we finish with this map, though, can I ask you to once again stand up and you'll see that I put two pins in the map. Now one of the pins, it's in just to the left of the middle and marks the village of Kozmatica, and the other one is placed at Colopek and that's to the right of the middle of the map. Can I ask you without speaking get up, take a look at those pins, where they are, and then return to your seat and I'll ask you a question. And perhaps if you can put your finger on the pin so the Chamber can see where ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Maybe if the usher could assist.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I don't see any pins.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I was unable to see any pins.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- don't sit down yet, please. Just walk over and keep the earphones on, please. Look to the middle of the map. Please keep the earphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, "Svedok." Could you please, Mr. Usher, draw the attention of the witness to -- yes. Please proceed, Mr. Groome. It means that everything is in control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So look at the middle of the map. And then if you just -- okay. Down a little bit lower. Now just look to the left there. Do you see the red pin sticking in the map? Just a little bit to the left. Just come straight towards the left. Okay? Your finger is now on Kozmatica. Now go down to the right of the middle of the map, a bit further south, go back to the middle of the map, and go to the right of the middle. Now you have your finger on Colopek. Now you've put your fingers on both. Okay? Now can you return to your seat. Look at the area in between those two pins and please then return to your seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No loud speaking, Mr. Mladic. No loud speaking. That's a simple instruction. If you want to communicate with counsel, either you write a little note or you whisper at such a level that you don't -- we cannot hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe -- what I was able to hear from Mr. Mladic is that he is unable to see and he's asking for the areas to be marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. There's nothing wrong in what he wishes to achieve at this moment. Mr. Groome, may I take it that you will invite the witness to make markings on the map on the screen now or not? Because Mr. Mladic was at such a distance that he couldn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where the pins are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: -- state for the record: Before court started today, Mr. Mladic did have an opportunity to come up to the map with Mr. Lukic. I asked Mr. Lukic to point out the two pins to him so he would know what we're talking about during this portion of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I certainly have no issue with Mr. Mladic during the next break coming back to look at these pins in this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. The Chamber was not aware that such an opportunity has been given to Mr. Mladic, but in view of that fact we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, my question to you is: Is the territory between those two pins - between Kozmatica and Colopek - that's area held by the VRS army; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to answer that question. I was the brigade commander. These questions fall exclusively within the competence of the corps command. I'd rather not answer those question, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's not your position. If you have any knowledge that that terrain between the two points you just indicated by looking at and pointing at the pins, if you know that this was under your control of your army, then you should answer the question irrespective of whether -- if you say I don't know, then that's a different matter. Then tell us that you don't know. But it's not because of your position that you should not answer the question. So do you know it or do you not know it? And if you want Mr. Groome to repeat the question, the question was -- yes, you know it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can answer the question conditionally only, because I can see on the map that there were no ABiH forces in between. So my answer would be I can see on the map that that part of territory was VRS controlled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you only know it from the maps. You had no idea that this in fact was terrain which was VRS controlled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do know that it was so, but I am unaware of precise details of the lines of separation. That is why I don't want to go any further into the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you know in global terms that that terrain approximately was under VRS control which is confirmed on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, the Chamber has heard other evidence that the two circles on this map represent the 20-kilometre exclusion zone that came into effect in February 1994. Does that agree with your understanding of what those circles are?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that it was the exclusion zone in terms of heavy artillery assets use; that is to say, our assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the radius of that circle is 20 kilometres and the diameter would be 40 kilometres; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Using that as a rough guide, would you agree with me that the distance between those two pins - between Kozmatica and Colopek - would be in excess of 20 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, but I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm finished with that map and now we're going to go with Rajlovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask that we look at -- load up P3 and go to e-court page 65.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
