utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, I'm going to -- as you've just heard me say, there is not a lot of video of this munition. I'm going to show you the remnants of the other type of modified aerial bomb to see whether you recognise this. So could I ask that we play 65 ter 30857a, and this is from video V000-4586, time code 1 minute 9 seconds to 1 minute 41 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: "It was surprising. It was a new Serb concoction, cobbled together from the engines of 122-millimetre rockets with a warhead designed to explode in the air. A highly inaccurate weapon designed solely to wreak terror on civilian areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: "They'd never seen anything like it before. It wasn't surprising. In was a new Serb concoction, cobbled together from the engines of 122-millimetre rockets with a warhead designed to explode in the air. A highly inaccurate weapon, designed solely to wreak terror on civilian areas."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, my question to you regarding this video is -- I'm not asking you to agree with the comments by the news reporter, but what I'm asking you is the type of frame that we see here that is -- has the remnants of the rockets attached, is this the type of apparatus that was used in the Ilidza Brigade to attach three rockets to a -- an air bomb? Is it similar to that type of apparatus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 30857a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I won't object to it on that basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the absence of any objection, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30857a receives number P6615, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P6615 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, sir, for the last thing I'd like to do with you today is to talk about the aiming of the air bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I think we'll be assisted if we call up 65 ter 30862, and these are some photos of rocket systems. So if we could call them up and look on the first page of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So, sir, this first image, do you agree with me that this is an image depicting the Plamen rocket system?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you see that red arrow. Am I correct in that that arrow is pointing to a turret which allows the azimuth of the rocket to be -- or the bearing of the rocket to be aimed. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could we advance to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I believe this is the Orkan system. Are you sufficiently familiar with the Orkan system that you would be able tell us whether this is in fact the Orkan system?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's Orkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And again if I can draw your attention to the red arrow, this is pointing to a turret, albeit a different design, that again allows the -- the bearing of the tubes to be adjusted; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The technical solution is somewhat different, but the principle is to actually adjust the bearing of the tubes and achieve a certain azimuth, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the two hydraulic pistons that we see on the side, that would be for adjusting the elevation of the tubes; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Based on the range that needs to be achieved, you use firing tables in order to adjust the pistons and achieve a certain elevation for the barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can we advance to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And this is a picture or a still from P6614, the video that we saw, and if I can draw your attention to the red arrow. And my question to you is: It is apparent from this that this launcher does not have a turret, it does not have a mechanism for adjusting the bearing of the rockets, does it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR RADOJCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it from here. Perhaps it is somewhere else, somewhere on the side. But if there is, we can't see from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, could I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that you get stuck in the middle of a --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I simply tender this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- firing position, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could tender this and I'll be done for the day, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the photographs uploaded under one number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They're all up on one number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 30862 receives number P6616, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. We adjourn for the day. Witness, I'd like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate in whatever other way about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given, and we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is certainly what I'm going do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you asked for six hours and I think you've used two and a half hours. So may I take it, Mr. Ivetic, that you would need some time as well for re-examination in view of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have approximately -- I'd say probably 20 to 25 minutes of questions already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that there's no fair chance that we would conclude the testimony of this witness tomorrow, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that we would resume to hear the testimony of this witness only next week, Wednesday, after tomorrow, because we're not sitting on Monday or Tuesday. We adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow, Friday, the 27th of June, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 27th day of June, 2014, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.19 p.m.,
